summary: Jeffrey Clark Ruff is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned his BA and MA from Missouri State University and his PhD from UC Santa Barbara under David Gordon White. He became an Assistant Professor at Marshall University in 2002.

Jeffrey Davis Schoening is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Washington (attested 1991) under doctoral supervisor Collett Cox and advisor Sanghasen Singh.

Jeffrey Hopkins (1940–2024) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and under Tenzin Gyatso, Ngawang Wangyal, and Geshe Lhundub Sopa, later serving as an Associate Professor at the University of Virginia (1973–2005).

Jeffrey J. Kripal (born 1962) specializes in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Conception Seminary College and earned his PhD from the University of Chicago, later becoming J. Newton Rayzor Chair and Religion Department chairman at Rice University around 2002.

Jeffrey K. Riegel (born 1945) is a scholar of Sinology and philosophy. He served as Professor of Chinese at the University of California, Berkeley from 1979 to 2007, and subsequently held a post at the University of Sydney from 2007 to 2017.

Jeffrey Kotyk specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He earned an MA from Komazawa University and a PhD from Leiden University under James A. Benn, later holding posts at McMaster University and the University of Bologna.

Jeffrey Mehlman (born 1944) is a scholar of philosophy and other fields. He held posts at Cornell University, Yale University, and Johns Hopkins University before becoming University Professor and Professor of French Literature at Boston University around 1984.

Jeffrey Moussaieff Masson (born 1941) is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who earned his BA and PhD at Harvard University under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He served at the University of Toronto and as Professor of Sanskrit at UC Berkeley (1981–1992).

Jeffrey Newmark is a scholar of Japanology and history/archaeology. He studied at Harvard University from approximately 1992 to 1996 and at the University of British Columbia from around 2002 to 2009, holding a post at the University of Winnipeg around 2009.

Jeffrey S. Lidke is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He held a post at Berry College and served as a visiting assistant professor of religion at the University of Virginia (attested 2003).

Jeffrey Samuels is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned his PhD from the University of Virginia under Karen Christina Lang and W. S. Karunatillake. He became Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Western Kentucky University (attested 2013).

Jeffrey Stout (born 1950) is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Brown University and earned his PhD from Princeton University, where he served as a professor from 1976 to 2018.

Jeffrey Wayne Bass is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at UNC Wilmington, the University of Tennessee, and UCLA, completing his PhD under Gregory Schopen. He has held teaching posts at UCLA and UC San Diego.

Jenkuan Shih is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 2006). Shih's studies were supervised by Charles Hallisey, Mark Csikszentmihalyi, and Geshe Lhundub Sopa.

Jens Braarvig (born 1948) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. In 2003, he held professor posts at the University of Oslo and the Norwegian Institute of Palaeography and Historical Philology.

Jens Peter Laut (born 1954) is a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He succeeded Klaus Röhrborn in 2008 and held a post at the University of Göttingen from around 2008 to 2020.

Jens Schlieter (born 1966) works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Bonn under Josef Simon and became Professor and Institute Director at the University of Bern around 2006.

Jens-Uwe Hartmann (born 1953) is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology who studied at the University of Munich and the University of Göttingen. He served as a professor at the University of Berlin and the University of Munich (1999–2018).

Jeong-Eun Kim is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. Kim earned a PhD from SOAS University of London in 2011, studying under doctoral supervisor Youngsook Pak and teacher Rosemary Smith.

Jerome Silbergeld (born 1944) is a scholar of Chinese art history and Sinology who earned his BA and PhD at Stanford. He held posts as Chair and Director at the University of Washington (1975–2001) and professor at Princeton University (2001–2018).
